Neither passage provides data on thermal conductivity, W–Cu interfaces, or irradiation resistance, so the key premises about interfacial thermal resistance reduction, mechanical/irradiation property retention, and the specific 20–30% conductivity gain are unsupported by the cited prior work.
premises: A nanometer-scale Cu or Ni interlayer on W particles reduces interfacial thermal resistance in W–Cu composites.
Electroless plating and vacuum annealing at ~900 °C produce a coherent, low-resistance W–Cu interface without deleterious intermetallics.
The interlayer preserves mechanical durability and irradiation resistance of the composite.
The interlayer increases thermal conductivity by 20–30% over an uncoated baseline.
